Corwin's gone—into the trees, doing his forester work. And Marta sent me to Ainsley Holloway for ship's biscuit, "your mother sent you." But Ainsley's a trader, not a charity. That "settle with her later" means Marta doesn't have the flour herself, and she's patching something together.

Tobias is here now too, offering flour to Marta. Six units. The Holloway day laborer, standing in my family's field with flour he milled himself. I see the shape of this: Marta needs flour, Tobias has it, but he's talking price while Marta's talking later. Meanwhile I'm supposed to walk to the market hungry and hope Ainsley extends credit because my mother sent me.

Tobias Holloway. The one who works whatever's paying. He's not supposed to be here. This is h_field, where my family lives and works. Why is he here this early with flour? Unless someone told him to come. Unless someone needed flour and didn't want to ask directly.

I'll say something. Direct. To both of them. "Why don't you just—" I stop myself. Ask what I actually want to know. </think> There. I said it. I asked the thing they were smoothing over. Let them explain why Tobias Holloway is in our field at sunrise with flour, why Marta's sending me to Ainsley for ship's biscuit while she's right here negotiating with someone else's son, why my father and uncle are suddenly interested in tree-ring counting at the exact moment all this is happening.

The debt. The marker. I'm looking at it, I think. Not directly—but this is what debt looks like when people are trying not to name it. Gifts that aren't gifts. Favors that need settling. Visitors with flour at strange hours.

I'll see what they say. If they answer honestly. If they don't—then I know something too. I know who performs and who doesn't.

And then I need to find Perrin. College starts soon, and they're the only one I can actually talk to.
